inShort: A dinks low to B's backhand, and B flicks it out of the air: wrist down, paddle tip down, then forward, not up. 10, then swap.
rules: A and B stand across from each other at the kitchen line. B holds a continental grip.
A dinks soft and low to B's backhand. B takes it out of the air, below net height.
Drop the wrist so the paddle tip points down. Keep the face only slightly open, a little more closed than feels natural.
Then go forward with the paddle, not up, and hit the ball straight.
A blocks the flick back softly or catches it, then feeds the next one.
tooEasy: A varies the height and depth of the dink; B still flicks only backhands. Even harder: A feeds faster, or calls a target.
tooHard: A feeds by hand from close range.
goodLooksLike: 7 of 10 flicks go low over the net into A's half, and none pops up.

drill.title: Backhand Flick out of the Dink (Gabe Tardio)
